> **Pipeline step 03 — TPS fork-length models (main text).**
>
> **Purpose.** Fit the 19 gaussian fork-length models (`fit_tps_fl_1` … `fit_tps_fl_19`) with a
> `(1 | StationCode)` intercept and score them with leave-one-station-out (K = 69) grouped
> cross-validation.
>
> **Inputs.** `data/tps_forklength_data.csv` (built by `00_data/01_build_model_datasets.Rmd`).
>
> **Outputs.** `fits_tps_fl_kfold/fit_tps_fl_<N>.rds`, K-fold sidecars `kfold69_tps_fl_<N>.rds`,
> `fits_tps_fl_kfold/fit_tps_fl_kfold69_comparisons.csv`.
>
> **Cost.** Long (69 refits per model); fitting chunks are `eval=FALSE`.

```{r project-root, include=FALSE}
# Every path in this notebook (data/, fits_*/, output_figs/, cache/) is relative to the
# REPOSITORY ROOT, not to this file's sub-folder. Walk up from the working directory to the
# folder holding the .Rproj file, and make knitr (and RStudio's chunk-by-chunk notebook
# mode) run every chunk from there. Base R only -- no extra package needed.
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(path)
  while (!length(list.files(p, pattern = "\\.Rproj$"))) {
    if (dirname(p) == p) stop("No .Rproj file found above ", path)
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  p
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = find_repo_root())
```
Fork-length analogue of `02_edsm_catch_models/edsm_catch_kfold_models.Rmd`. We fit every fork-length model
`fit_tps_fl_1` .. `fit_tps_fl_19` (gaussian, with a `(1|StationCode)` random intercept) and score
them with grouped (by StationCode) K-fold CV instead of PSIS-LOO. Folds are grouped on StationCode
because that is the random-intercept variable. Unlike the trawl notebook this starts from scratch:
we generate and cache the fold set ourselves rather than recovering it from previously fit models.

K choice: there are 69 stations, so K = 69 is leave-one-station-out (LOSO); K = 10 is much faster.
Every Edge_Type level spans >= 5 stations, so LOSO is always safe for the Edge_Type models; the
fold builder checks factor-level coverage and warns if a smaller K ever splits a level into one fold.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(brms)
library(rstan)
library(loo)
library(future)

options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
```

Config — set the number of grouped-by-station folds here (single source of truth).
```{r}
K_FOLDS  <- 69   # 69 = leave-one-station-out (safest); set to 10 for a much faster run
FIT_DIR  <- "fits_tps_fl_kfold"
if (!dir.exists(FIT_DIR)) dir.create(FIT_DIR, recursive = TRUE)
```

Load fork-length dataset (ready to go — no further wrangling needed).
```{r}
d_fl <- read_csv("data/tps_forklength_data.csv")
d_fl$Edge_Type   <- factor(d_fl$Edge_Type)     # 5-level factor predictor
d_fl$StationCode <- factor(d_fl$StationCode)   # 69 grouping levels
```

Prior (same as the source fork-length analysis).
```{r}
fl_priors <- c(set_prior("normal(0,5)", class = "b"))
```


###################################
Station-level K-fold helper.
The fold assignment is supplied as a precomputed vector (`folds`) so that EVERY model is scored
on the exact same partition of stations — this is what makes the K-fold comparison valid.
Settings: gaussian, iter = 4000 / warmup = 2000 (2000 draws), adapt_delta = 0.95
(diagnostic-checked: 0 divergences, Rhat <= 1.02 on both the base and full-covariate models).
########################################
```{r}
add_station_kfold <- function(
  fit,
  folds,
  K,
  group   = "StationCode",
  chains  = 4,
  cores   = 4,
  iter    = 4000,
  warmup  = 2000,
  control = list(max_treedepth = 10, adapt_delta = 0.95),
  seed    = 123,
  save_fits = FALSE
) {
  stopifnot(length(folds) == nrow(fit$data))
  set.seed(seed)

  kf <- brms::kfold(
    fit,
    folds   = folds,        # custom fold vector -> identical partition for every model
    compare = FALSE,
    save_fits = save_fits,
    chains  = chains,
    cores   = cores,
    iter    = iter,
    warmup  = warmup,
    control = control
  )

  # Stored under e.g. "kfold69_StationCode" so the comparison code can find it.
  fit$criteria[[paste0("kfold", K, "_", group)]] <- kf
  fit
}
```


###################################
Fold-partition builder.
Creates the grouped-by-StationCode fold vector ONCE for a given K, caches it to disk, and checks
that no factor level (Edge_Type) lands entirely in a single fold (which would break kfold for the
models that use it). Returns an integer fold id (1..K) per row, aligned to `data` row order.
########################################
```{r}
# Warn if any factor level appears in only one fold (training would then lack that level).
check_factor_coverage <- function(data, folds, factors = "Edge_Type") {
  for (f in intersect(factors, names(data))) {
    n_folds_with_level <- rowSums(table(level = data[[f]], fold = folds) > 0)
    bad <- names(which(n_folds_with_level < 2))
    if (length(bad)) {
      warning("Factor '", f, "' level(s) {", paste(bad, collapse = ", "),
              "} appear in only one fold -> kfold will fail for models using '", f,
              "'. Use a larger K (K = 69 / LOSO is always safe here) or a different seed.")
    } else {
      message("Factor '", f, "' coverage OK (every level spans >= 2 folds).")
    }
  }
}

make_station_folds <- function(data, K, group = "StationCode",
                               factors = "Edge_Type", seed = 123, dir = FIT_DIR) {
  file <- file.path(dir, sprintf("kfold%d_station_folds.rds", K))
  if (file.exists(file)) {
    folds <- readRDS(file)
  } else {
    set.seed(seed)
    folds <- as.integer(loo::kfold_split_grouped(K = K, x = factor(data[[group]])))
    stopifnot(length(folds) == nrow(data))
    if (!dir.exists(dir)) dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE)
    saveRDS(folds, file)
  }
  check_factor_coverage(data, folds, factors)
  folds
}
```


###################################
Model definition table + runner.
`fit_defs` lists the fixed-effects part of each model (fit 1..19), transcribed from
`tidal-parr-forklength-analysis2.rmd`. The base model appended to each is:
  ForkLength ~ <fixef> + water_year_day_z + (1|StationCode)
########################################
```{r}
# Fixed-effects part of each model ("" = base model: water_year_day_z + intercept only).
fit_defs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~num, ~fixef,
  1L,   "",
  2L,   "distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z + start_depth_z",
  3L,   "distance_m_z + start_depth_z",
  4L,   "distance_along_channel_z + start_depth_z",
  5L,   "distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z",
  6L,   "distance_along_channel_z",
  7L,   "distance_m_z",
  8L,   "start_depth_z",
  9L,   "distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z + start_depth_z + out30_z",
  10L,  "distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z + start_depth_z + Edge_Type",
  11L,  "distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z + start_depth_z + Edge_Type + out30_z",
  12L,  "distance_m_z + start_depth_z + out30_z",
  13L,  "distance_m_z + start_depth_z + out30_z + Edge_Type",
  14L,  "Edge_Type",
  15L,  "distance_along_channel_z + Edge_Type",
  16L,  "distance_m_z + Edge_Type",
  17L,  "start_depth_z + Edge_Type",
  18L,  "distance_m_z + start_depth_z + Edge_Type",
  19L,  "distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z + Edge_Type"
)

# Build the full brms formula for a given fixed-effects string.
build_fl_formula <- function(fixef) {
  rhs <- c(fixef, "water_year_day_z", "(1|StationCode)")
  rhs <- rhs[nzchar(trimws(rhs))]          # drop empty fixef (base model)
  as.formula(paste("ForkLength ~", paste(rhs, collapse = " + ")))
}

# Fit ONE model, run station K-fold on the cached folds, save the fit + a lightweight kfold
# sidecar (the part needed for ELPD ranking / ensemble weights), append the summary, free memory.
# save_pars(all = FALSE) keeps b_*, sd_StationCode, sigma and r_StationCode -> enough for
# conditional effects, CIs, and beta forest plots; only the moment-matching extras are dropped.
fit_fl_model <- function(num, fixef, folds, K,
                         data    = d_fl,
                         priors  = fl_priors,
                         iter    = 4000,
                         warmup  = 2000,
                         chains  = 4,
                         control = list(max_treedepth = 10, adapt_delta = 0.95),
                         dir     = FIT_DIR) {
  form <- build_fl_formula(fixef)
  message("=== Fitting fit_tps_fl_", num, " ===")
  print(form)

  fit <- brm(
    formula = form,
    family  = gaussian(),
    data    = data,
    prior   = priors,
    iter    = iter, warmup = warmup, chains = chains,
    control = control,
    save_pars = save_pars(all = FALSE)
  )

  fit <- add_station_kfold(
    fit = fit, folds = folds, K = K,
    chains = chains, iter = iter, warmup = warmup, control = control
  )

  # Full fit (posterior draws -> conditional effects / CIs / forest plots)
  saveRDS(fit, file = file.path(dir, sprintf("fit_tps_fl_%d.rds", num)))
  # Lightweight kfold criterion (ELPD -> ranking / ensemble weights) without loading the big fit
  saveRDS(fit$criteria[[paste0("kfold", K, "_StationCode")]],
          file = file.path(dir, sprintf("kfold%d_tps_fl_%d.rds", K, num)))

  # Printout to the designated txt file
  fileConn <- file(file.path(dir, "fit_tps_fl_output.txt"), open = "a")
  cat(sprintf("\n\n\nSummary of fit_tps_fl_%d:\n\n", num), file = fileConn)
  cat(capture.output(summary(fit)), file = fileConn, sep = "\n")
  close(fileConn)

  rm(fit); gc()
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Loop over a set of fit numbers (default: all 19).
run_fl_fits <- function(nums = fit_defs$num, K = K_FOLDS, defs = fit_defs,
                        folds = station_folds, ...) {
  unknown <- setdiff(nums, defs$num)
  if (length(unknown)) {
    stop("No fixed-effects definition for fit number(s): ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "))
  }
  for (num in nums) {
    fixef <- defs$fixef[match(num, defs$num)]
    fit_fl_model(num = num, fixef = fixef, folds = folds, K = K, ...)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
```


###################################
Core-aware parallelism (same approach as the trawl notebook).
Folds are parallelized across `workers`; each fold still runs `chains` chains, and we never
oversubscribe: workers = floor(cores / chains). chains stays 4 on every machine.
########################################
```{r}
kfold_workers <- function(chains = 4) {
  nc <- parallel::detectCores()
  if (is.na(nc)) nc <- 1L
  max(1L, nc %/% chains)
}

# Set the future plan brms::kfold uses to dispatch folds. Call once before running.
# Pass workers = 1 to force sequential if nested parallelism misbehaves on macOS.
setup_kfold_plan <- function(chains = 4, workers = NULL) {
  library(future)
  options(future.globals.maxSize = 3 * 1024^3)
  if (is.null(workers)) workers <- kfold_workers(chains)
  if (workers >= 2L) plan(multisession, workers = workers) else plan(sequential)
  message(sprintf("Cores: %s | chains/fold: %d | fold-workers: %d (%s)",
                  parallel::detectCores(), chains, workers,
                  if (workers >= 2L) "folds run in parallel" else "folds run sequentially"))
  invisible(workers)
}
```


###################################
Runtime check (optional).
Times a short pilot fit on the real model + data, then extrapolates to one full fit + K-fold and
to the whole batch. Defaults to K = 69 (LOSO). Auto-detects cores so the estimate reflects how
`setup_kfold_plan()` will actually run. Does NOT run a full fit.
########################################
```{r eval=FALSE}
estimate_fl_time <- function(fixef       = "distance_m_z + start_depth_z",
                             nW          = 500L, nDraw = 250L,    # pilot iters
                             prod_warmup = 2000, prod_sample = 2000,
                             K = 69, chains = 4, n_models = 19,
                             workers = NULL,
                             data = d_fl, priors = fl_priors) {
  if (is.null(workers)) workers <- kfold_workers(chains)

  pilot <- brm(
    build_fl_formula(fixef),
    family = gaussian(), data = data, prior = priors,
    chains = 1, warmup = nW, iter = nW + nDraw,
    control = list(max_treedepth = 10, adapt_delta = 0.95),
    refresh = 0, seed = 1
  )

  et     <- rstan::get_elapsed_time(pilot$fit)         # per-chain warmup / sample seconds
  Tchain <- (et[1, "warmup"] / nW)   * prod_warmup +   # extrapolate to production iters
            (et[1, "sample"] / nDraw) * prod_sample
  waves      <- ceiling(K / workers)                   # k-fold runs in this many sequential waves
  kfold_wall <- waves * ((K - 1) / K) * Tchain         # each fold trains on ~ (K-1)/K of the rows
  per_model  <- Tchain + kfold_wall                    # main fit (chains in parallel) + k-fold

  cat(sprintf("cores=%s  chains=%d  fold-workers=%d  K=%d  ->  %d k-fold wave(s)\n",
              parallel::detectCores(), chains, workers, K, waves))
  cat(sprintf("single full fit : %5.1f min\n", Tchain / 60))
  cat(sprintf("one model       : %5.1f min  (%.2f h)\n", per_model / 60, per_model / 3600))
  cat(sprintf("%2d models        : %5.1f h\n", n_models, n_models * per_model / 3600))
  invisible(per_model)
}

estimate_fl_time(K = 69)    # leave-one-station-out
estimate_fl_time(K = 10)    # the faster alternative
```


###################################
Build / cache the fold set for the chosen K.
########################################
```{r}
station_folds <- make_station_folds(d_fl, K = K_FOLDS)
table(station_folds)
```


###################################
Run the fits.
Each fit + K-fold is slow at K = 69; run this interactively, not on knit.
########################################
```{r eval=FALSE}
# Auto-detect cores and parallelize folds (8 cores -> 2 at a time; 4 cores -> sequential).
setup_kfold_plan(chains = 4)

station_folds <- make_station_folds(d_fl, K = K_FOLDS)

# Run all 19 (or pass a subset, e.g. run_fl_fits(c(1, 9, 11))).
run_fl_fits(nums = 1:19, K = K_FOLDS)
```


###################################
Reload K-fold results and rank models by ELPD.
Reads the lightweight kfold sidecars (fast — no need to load the full fits), runs loo_compare,
and writes the ranking. Re-run any time after more fits finish.
########################################
```{r eval=FALSE}
fit_nums <- 1:19

kfold_results <- list()
for (num in fit_nums) {
  f <- file.path(FIT_DIR, sprintf("kfold%d_tps_fl_%d.rds", K_FOLDS, num))
  if (file.exists(f)) {
    kfold_results[[paste0("fit_tps_fl_", num)]] <- readRDS(f)
  }
}

if (length(kfold_results) < 2) {
  stop("Need at least two fits with K = ", K_FOLDS, " kfold results to compare.")
}

# ELPD comparison ranking (best model on top, elpd_diff relative to it)
kfold_comparisons_fl <- loo_compare(kfold_results)
print(kfold_comparisons_fl)

write.csv(
  as.data.frame(kfold_comparisons_fl),
  file.path(FIT_DIR, sprintf("fit_tps_fl_kfold%d_comparisons.csv", K_FOLDS))
)
```
